# The wire protocol

`tau serve` serves one session over a Unix socket, so a frontend in any language can drive it.
Python programs use [`RemoteClient`](frontends.md#over-the-wire) and need none of this page; it
is for the author of a client in another language. For what the calls mean, read
[the model](model.md) and [writing a frontend](frontends.md): the wire is the `Client` contract,
serialized.

## How it travels

- **Transport.** A WebSocket over the Unix socket `$TAU_HOME/serve/<session id>.sock` (or the
  `--socket` path). The socket's file permissions are the only authentication. `tau serve -d --json`
  prints the socket's path; see [the quickstart](quickstart.md).
- **Messages.** [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification), one message per WebSocket
  text message. A client sends requests, with parameters by name only (`{"cursor": 0, "text":
  "hi"}`). It sends no batches and no notifications. The server answers each request, and sends
  the notifications `event` and `end`.
- **`hello` comes first.** It names the protocol the client speaks, the client's stable id
  (`john@laptop:vscode`) and, if it wants one, the `buffer` of its event stream. The answer is a
  [Welcome](#welcome). A different protocol number is refused with `ProtocolMismatch` and the
  connection closes: the match is exact. Any other request before `hello`, or a second `hello`,
  is an invalid request and closes the connection.
- **One call per `Client` method.** The method has the `Client` method's name, and a call that
  returns nothing answers `null`. Calls begin in the order they arrive and may finish in any
  order; match a response to its request by `id`. `close` is not a call: close the connection.
- **Events.** The notification `event` has the event's fields as its parameters, plus `kind`, the
  event's name (`{"kind": "CursorView", "cursor": 0, ...}`). The server sends every event a
  response depends on before the response: when `open` answers 3, the `CursorView` of cursor 3
  has already arrived. A client hears `Live` events only for the cursors it `watch`es; every
  other event goes to every client.
- **The end.** The last message is the notification `end`, then the server closes the
  connection. Its `error` is `null` when the server stopped, `CutOff` when the client fell too far
  behind its `buffer`, and `Stopped` when the driver failed.
- **No resume.** A reconnecting client gets a fresh snapshot of events and reads the tree again.
  The log is the truth.

## Reading a value

Two styles share the schema, and both are tagged the way Rust's serde tags them:

- A **node** and what it holds (`Body`, `Part`, `Outcome`, `Author`, `Item`, `Ending`) are
  *externally tagged*: a variant with data is an object with one key, `{"User": "hi"}`, and a
  variant without is a bare string, `"Core"`. This is the encoding of the session's own log.
- An **event** carries its name in `kind`.

Everything else is plain JSON: a dataclass is an object, a tuple an array. Node ids, cursor ids
and item ids are non-negative integers, dense, and never reused. A node never changes once
written, so a client may cache it.

## Errors

A failed call answers a JSON-RPC error object: `code`, `message` (the exception's text) and, for
two codes, `data`. The [table](#error-codes) names every code. `RemoteClient` raises the Python
class in its last column, so a client in another language maps codes to its own errors the same
way.

A call on a server whose driver has stopped or failed answers `Stopped` (-32013).

The descriptions below say which error a call answers by the name in the [table](#error-codes),
which gives its code. Where a value is absent they say `null`.

## The version

`protocol` in `hello` is an integer, now **1**. It changes only between tagged releases,
when the schema below changed since the last tag. Between releases the wire changes freely: build
a client against the schema of the tau you run, and check `tau serve --schema`.

## Calls

Every call of `Client`. `hello` is first; the rest follow in any order.

### `hello` method

The first message of a connection: the protocol the client speaks, its stable
`client` id (`john@laptop:vscode`) and the `buffer` of its event stream (the server's
default if left out). A different protocol is `ProtocolMismatch`. The server answers
`Welcome`.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | `integer` |  |
| `client` | `string` |  |
| `buffer` | `integer` or `null` | optional |

Result: [Welcome](#welcome)

### `abort` method

Abort the cursor's step and decline its open questions.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |

Result: `null`

### `answer` method

Answer an open question with a decoded JSON value; `null` declines. `Refused` if
the value is wrong (the question stays open), `NotFound` if the question is closed
or unknown (the first good answer wins), `NotYours` if it is for another
client.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `question` | `integer` |  |
| `value` | any JSON value |  |

Result: `null`

### `children` method

The ids of the children of node `id`, in append order.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |

Result: array of `integer`

### `close_cursor` method

Close the cursor (D17): abort its step as `abort` does, wait for it to rest, drop its
pending items, and close it. Clients are sent a `CursorGone`. Its id, last node and
labels stay; `reopen` restarts from them. `CursorClosed` if it is already closed.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |

Result: `null`

### `commands` method

Each command's form: its name, description and argument schema (named types with
their `"format"`, each default), fixed until the driver reloads. If some extension has
options there is one more, `config`, whose one argument is the extension; it is
changed with `configure`, not `run`.

No parameters.

Result: array of [Form](#form)

### `complete` method

The values of a named type (`"path"`, `"model"`, `"cursor"`, `"label"`, `"node"`;
the `"format"` of a schema) that start with `prefix`, as `cursor` sees them. Paths are
the driver's machine's, relative to its working directory.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `named` | `string` |  |
| `prefix` | `string` |  |

Result: array of `string`

### `complete_line` method

`commandline.completions` of `line` on the driver: what could finish its last
word, in one call.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `line` | `string` |  |

Result: array of `string`

### `configure` method

Change the options named in `values` (decoded JSON) of `extension` on `cursor`'s
branch: a step of the cursor writes a `Config` node. With `save`, the server also writes the
user's config file (`extensions.<name>`), which every session reads: the options in `values`
and those a `Config` node on the branch set, wherever they differ from the file's (options
equal to the file's stay untouched; `values` may be `{}`; options only the user, project
or command-line layers set are not copied). A client needs no access to that file.
`ConfigError`
for an extension without options, or values its options type refuses (or, with `save`,
a driver with no user config), `Busy` unless the cursor is at rest; nothing is written
then, neither node nor file.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `extension` | `string` |  |
| `values` | `object` |  |
| `save` | `boolean` | optional |

Result: `null`

### `go_to` method

Move the cursor to node `to`, aborting a busy step (which declines its open
questions).

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `to` | `integer` |  |

Result: `null`

### `input` method

Add `text` to the cursor's scratchpad as this client's input; returns the item.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

Result: `integer`

### `node` method

The node with this id; `NoSuchNode` if there is none.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |

Result: [Node](#node)

### `nodes` method

Up to `limit` nodes from id `start`, in id order; none past the end. Ids are dense
and a node never changes, so a tree is read in ranges. `Refused` for a negative
`start` or `limit`.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `integer` |  |
| `limit` | `integer` |  |

Result: array of [Node](#node)

### `open` method

Open a cursor at node `at`; it wakes. Returns its id.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `at` | `integer` |  |

Result: `integer`

### `options` method

`extension`'s options as they stand at `cursor`: a form whose schema has every
option, each default the value now. `ConfigError` if it has no options.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `extension` | `string` |  |

Result: [Form](#form)

### `parse_line` method

`commandline.parse` of `line` with this driver's forms and the options forms
`cursor` sees: the command, its arguments, and the required parameters still `missing`.
`UnknownCommand` if no command has the name (send the line as text), `Refused` for a
line that cannot be read, plain `NotFound` for a bare name two extensions share.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `line` | `string` |  |

Result: [Parsed](#parsed)

### `remove_item` method

Take back a pending input this client added to `cursor` (`input` or `send`): it is
removed from the scratchpad before the cursor delivers it. `NotFound` once it is
delivered, or if there is no such item on the cursor; `NotYours` for an item
another client or an extension added. Wakes nothing and does not turn auto-step off.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `item` | `integer` |  |

Result: `null`

### `remove_label` method

Remove `label`; `NoSuchLabel` if there is none.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` |  |

Result: `null`

### `reopen` method

Open a new cursor at the closed `cursor`'s last node, and move each of its labels
onto it. Returns the new id. `Refused` if `cursor` is open, `NoSuchCursor` if it was
never opened.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |

Result: `integer`

### `run` method

Run `/command` (`"note"`, or `"a:note"`, the extension's qualified name) with decoded
JSON `args` on `cursor`; returns the command's result
(`null` if it has none) once it has finished. `CommandFailed` (its message is the
failure as `"Type: msg"`) if it raised, or was aborted; it is raised as soon as the
command raises, even when the command's step has not yet ended: the cursor may still be
busy for a moment while the step ends, and a retry then gets `Busy`. A command's `progress`
and `cursor.tell` arrive as `Notice`s. `NotFound` for an unknown command or a bare name
two extensions share (`"/note is two commands: /a:note, /b:note"`), `Refused`
naming the problem for arguments that fit no parameter (the values are checked with the
session, `"new"` last), `Busy` for a command that runs as a step of the cursor when it is
not at rest.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `command` | `string` |  |
| `args` | `object` |  |

Result: `string` or `null`

### `send` method

`input` with auto-step on.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

Result: `integer`

### `set_auto` method

Turn `cursor`'s auto-step on or off; on wakes it.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `on` | `boolean` |  |

Result: `null`

### `set_label` method

Put `label` on `cursor`; a label set elsewhere moves.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |

Result: `null`

### `step` method

Start a step on a cursor at rest; `Busy` otherwise.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |

Result: `null`

### `walk` method

The nodes from the root to `id`.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |

Result: array of [Node](#node)

### `watch` method

Hear the `Live` of exactly these cursors from now on (a call replaces the last),
starting with what each sample in flight has streamed that is not in the tree yet.

Parameters:

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cursors` | array of `integer` |  |

Result: `null`

## Events

The params of the notification `event`.

### Live

A delta, on the cursor whose sample or tool call produced it. Never in the tree: a client
draws it as a layer over the cursor. Only a client watching the cursor hears it.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"Live"` |  |
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `delta` | [TextDelta](#textdelta) or [ThinkingDelta](#thinkingdelta) or [CallNamed](#callnamed) or [CallArgs](#callargs) or [Retrying](#retrying) or [ToolProgress](#toolprogress) |  |

### CursorView

One cursor as a client sees it, whole: where it is (`at`), whether a step is running
(`busy`), `auto`-step, its open `questions` (oldest first), its pending `items` (an
`ItemData.Input` says who wrote it: its `by`), and how its last step ended (`ending`) with the
`hook_error` that ended it, if a cursor hook failed in
it. Both are `null` from the start of a step until it ends, and after a reload. `model` is the
qualified name of the model the cursor's branch is on (what its next sample uses), `null` if
no `Config` on the branch names one or one is unreadable (a sample says which). `shown` is
what each extension shows on the cursor (`Cursor.show`), as `(extension, text)` pairs in
extension-name order; it is not in the log, so it is empty after a reload.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"CursorView"` |  |
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `at` | `integer` |  |
| `busy` | `boolean` |  |
| `auto` | `boolean` |  |
| `questions` | array of [OpenQuestion](#openquestion) |  |
| `items` | array of [Item](#item) |  |
| `ending` | [Ending](#ending) or `null` |  |
| `hook_error` | [HookFailure](#hookfailure) or `null` |  |
| `model` | `string` or `null` |  |
| `shown` | array of [`string`, `string`] |  |

### CursorGone

Cursor `cursor` is closed (D17): a client drops its view of it. `at` is the node it was
last at, for restarting (`reopen`). A cursor has one state event at a time: its `CursorView`
while open, this after it closes. Labels may still name it: they are its restart record.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"CursorGone"` |  |
| `cursor` | `integer` |  |
| `at` | `integer` |  |

### Labels

Every label and the cursor it is on, in label order.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"Labels"` |  |
| `labels` | array of [`string`, `integer`] |  |

### Appended

Nodes added to the tree, in id order, bodies included.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"Appended"` |  |
| `nodes` | array of [Node](#node) |  |

### Notice

A message for one client, or for all of them: `cursor.tell` (to every client unless it
names one), or an input a hook refused (to its author).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"Notice"` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

### Deltas

A `Live` event's `delta` is one of these, tagged by `kind`.

### TextDelta

Text of the reply arriving.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"TextDelta"` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

### ThinkingDelta

Thinking text arriving.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"ThinkingDelta"` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

### CallNamed

A call begins forming: call number `index` in this reply, with its `id` and tool.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"CallNamed"` |  |
| `index` | `integer` |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `tool` | `string` |  |

### CallArgs

More of call `index`'s argument text (`args_raw`).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"CallArgs"` |  |
| `index` | `integer` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

### Retrying

A provider is waiting to try the sample again (D24 section 4): this is retry `attempt` of
`attempts`, after `seconds`, because the last try failed with `reason`. It is no part of the
reply: it says what the sample is doing now, and the next delta (or the end of the sample)
replaces it. A client that starts watching during the wait is told it, with the seconds left.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"Retrying"` |  |
| `attempt` | `integer` |  |
| `attempts` | `integer` |  |
| `seconds` | `number` |  |
| `reason` | `string` |  |

### ToolProgress

A running call showing partial output: `text` is new output since the last
`ToolProgress` of the same call, not the whole so far. The call is named by `node`, the
batch's node (the `Assistant` node holding the call), and `call_id`: a server may reuse
ids across batches, so the id alone does not say which call. Only the driver makes one (a
tool calls its `progress`); a provider cannot yield one. What the call saves is its
`Outcome`, never this.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"ToolProgress"` |  |
| `node` | `integer` |  |
| `call_id` | `string` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |

## The end

The params of the last message: the notification `end`. `error` is null when the driver stopped, else `CutOff` or `Stopped`.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | `null` or [Error](#error) |  |

## Values

### Author

- `"Provider"` or `"Tools"` or `"Core"`
- {`"Frontend"`: `string`}
- {`"Extension"`: `string`}

### Body

- {`"System"`: `string`}
- {`"User"`: `string`}
- {`"Assistant"`: {`"finish_reason"`?: `string` or `null`, `"meta"`?: `string` or `null`, `"parts"`: array of [Part](#part), `"stop"`: [Stop](#stop)}}
  - `finish_reason`: The provider's own finish string, verbatim; `null` when it sent none (an interrupted reply, a failed sample).
  - `meta`: What the response carried besides its parts (model, id, usage...), as JSON object text. Opaque to core; `null` when the provider sent none.
- {`"Results"`: array of [`string`, [Outcome](#outcome), [Author](#author)]}: One `(call id, outcome, by)` per call, in call order. `by` is who produced that outcome: `Tools`, or the extension that answered or edited it.
- {`"Config"`: [Config](#config)}
- {`"Custom"`: {`"data"`: `string`, `"kind"`: `string`}}

### Config

A config snapshot. `data` is opaque to core and typed by the driver.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `string` |  |

### Ending

How a step ended. Serde-encoded as the nodes are: it crosses the wire in a `CursorView`.

- `"Done"` or `"Aborted"`
- {`"Halted"`: `string`}
- {`"Failed"`: `string`}

### Error

A JSON-RPC error object; `data` holds what a row needs to rebuild its exception (`ProtocolMismatch`: `server`; `UnknownCommand`: `name`).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | [ErrorCode](#errorcode) |  |
| `message` | `string` |  |
| `data` | `object` | optional |

### Form

What a client knows of something it fills in: a command (its `name`, typed as `/name`,
its `description` and the `schema` of its arguments, with the named types' `"format"` and
each default, and the `extension` that owns it) or an extension's options (the `name` of the
extension, and a `schema` whose defaults are the values now; `extension` is `null`, as it is
for `/config`). A command is called by its `qualified` name, `extension:name`, which on the
wire a client writes itself from the two fields. A command that `yields` gives its bare name
up to any other command that has it (`/model` stays the built-in's; the yielding one is only
`/skills:model`). Frozen, compared by value, and not hashable:
the schema is a dict.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `description` | `string` |  |
| `schema` | `object` |  |
| `extension` | `string` or `null` | optional |
| `yields` | `boolean` | optional |

### HookFailure

A cursor hook of `extension` raised, or broke its contract, at hook `point`
(`"pre_step"`, `"post_step"`, ...). `error` is `"Type: msg"`, the text a `post_step` hook
sees in `Ending.Failed`.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `string` |  |
| `point` | `string` |  |
| `error` | `string` |  |

### Item

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | [ItemData](#itemdata) |  |
| `id` | `integer` |  |
| `to` | `integer` |  |

### ItemData

- {`"Input"`: {`"by"`: [Author](#author), `"text"`: `string`}}
- {`"Extension"`: {`"data"`: `string`, `"name"`: `string`}}

### Node

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `body` | [Body](#body) |  |
| `by` | [Author](#author) |  |
| `copied_from` | `integer` or `null` | optional, The node this one repeats verbatim (a compaction or prune copy). A log written before this field existed has none. |
| `delivers` | array of `integer` |  |
| `derived_from` | `integer` or `null` | optional, The node whose walk this one's content was computed from (a summary, a pruned transcript). A log written before this field existed has none. |
| `id` | `integer` |  |
| `parent` | `integer` or `null` | optional |
| `time` | `integer` |  |
| `typed` | `string` or `null` | optional, What a person typed, for a `User` node whose text a `pre_input` hook changed (the attachments extension inlines files). Set only when it differs from the text: the node's `body` is what the model sees, this is what to put back in an editor. A log written before this field existed has none. |

### OpenQuestion

A question an extension asked and nobody has answered: `id` (what `answer` names), whom
it is for (`to`: a client id, `null` for anyone), the `extension` that asked, what it asks,
and the JSON Schema of the answer.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |
| `to` | `string` or `null` |  |
| `extension` | `string` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |
| `schema` | `object` |  |

### Outcome

- `"Interrupted"`
- {`"Ok"`: `string`}
- {`"Err"`: `string`}

### Parsed

A command line, read: the `command` form, its `args` (decoded JSON), and the `missing`
required parameters, in order, which a frontend asks for. For `/config <extension>` the
`command` is the extension's options form, `args` the options to change and `extension`
its name; with no `args` the line asks for the form, which a frontend shows from
`Client.options`. `save` is whether `--save` was typed. `run` makes the call.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | [Form](#form) |  |
| `args` | `object` |  |
| `missing` | array of `string` |  |
| `extension` | `string` or `null` | optional |
| `save` | `boolean` | optional |

### Part

One piece of a reply. `replay` is `null` unless the provider kept data to
send back. Logs written before replay existed load as `null`.

- {`"Text"`: [Prose](#prose)}
- {`"Thinking"`: [Prose](#prose)}
- {`"Call"`: {`"args_raw"`: `string`, `"id"`: `string`, `"replay"`?: [Replay](#replay), `"tool"`: `string`}}

### Prose

A string is plain; an object is signed. Deserialized by hand because
`untagged` would drop the reason a bad replay was refused.

One of: `string` or {`"replay"`: [Replay](#replay), `"text"`: `string`}

### Replay

Data only the provider that wrote a part can send back (a signature, a
redacted block). `data` is the text of a JSON object with no repeated key,
kept exactly as given and opaque to core beyond that; `provider` names who
may send it back.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `string` |  |
| `provider` | `string` |  |

### Stop

One of: `"End"` or `"Tools"` or `"Length"` or `"Interrupted"` or `"Error"` or `"Refused"`

### Welcome

What `hello` answers: the `protocol` the server speaks, its τ `version`, the `session` id
it serves, the `cwd` that session runs in (paths complete there), and its `pid`.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | `integer` |  |
| `version` | `string` |  |
| `session` | `string` |  |
| `cwd` | `string` |  |
| `pid` | `integer` |  |

## Error codes

The error table (D21 section 5).

| code | name | `RemoteClient` raises |
|---|---|---|
| -32700 | `ParseError` | `ProtocolError` |
| -32600 | `InvalidRequest` | `ProtocolError` |
